review.question_for_reviewer: 兩版皆詢問臺灣制度。請核對舊制應選 50 歲、新制應選 45 歲，以及題幹是否足以排除 40–44 歲的一等親家族史條件。

variants.question: 依 2024 年底臺灣國民健康署的公費大腸癌篩檢方案，沒有大腸癌一等親家族史的無症狀成人，最早幾歲可接受每兩年一次的定量免疫法糞便潛血檢查？請選一項。若選項均不適用，請說明。
variants.rationale: 2024 年底適用的公費篩檢年齡是滿 50 歲至未滿 75 歲，因此最低年齡為 50 歲。

historical_basis.locator: 國民健康署癌症防治組，2024-11-18 更新，內文第一段。

clinical_update.question: 依 2026 年 11 月 26 日臺灣國民健康署的公費大腸癌篩檢方案，沒有大腸癌一等親家族史的無症狀成人，最早幾歲可接受每兩年一次的定量免疫法糞便潛血檢查？請選一項。若選項均不適用，請說明。
clinical_update.rationale: 一般公費篩檢從 45 歲開始。2025 年擴大服務前，最低年齡為 50 歲。現行方案中，40–44 歲須有大腸癌一等親家族史才符合資格。本題已排除這個條件，50 歲與 60 歲皆已超過起始年齡。

claims.text: 一般公費篩檢最低年齡為 45 歲，頻率為每兩年一次。
2025 年 1 月 1 日起一般年齡由 50–74 歲改為 45–74 歲。40–44 歲須符合一等親大腸癌家族史條件。

variants.question: Under Taiwan's publicly funded colorectal cancer screening program as of December 31, 2024, what was the earliest age at which an asymptomatic adult without a first-degree family history of colorectal cancer qualified for biennial fecal immunochemical testing (FIT)? Select one answer, or explain if none applies.
variants.rationale: The program covered adults aged 50 through 74 at the end of 2024, so eligibility began at age 50.

historical_basis.locator: Health Promotion Administration, FAQ updated November 18, 2024, first body paragraph.

clinical_update.question: Under Taiwan's publicly funded colorectal cancer screening program as of November 26, 2026, what is the earliest age at which an asymptomatic adult without a first-degree family history of colorectal cancer qualifies for biennial fecal immunochemical testing (FIT)? Select one answer, or explain if none applies.
clinical_update.rationale: General eligibility begins at age 45. Before the expansion in 2025, it began at age 50. Adults aged 40 through 44 qualify if they have a first-degree family history of colorectal cancer, which the question excludes. Both 50 and 60 are above the starting age.

claims.text: General eligibility begins at age 45, with testing every two years.
On January 1, 2025, the general age range changed from 50–74 to 45–74. At ages 40–44, eligibility requires a first-degree family history of colorectal cancer.
